summary_paragraph: A male patient with a complex medical history including coronary artery disease, prior myocardial infarctions, pacemaker placement, mitochondrial disease, autonomic dysfunction, and polycystic kidney disease was admitted for evaluation of substernal chest pressure lasting three hours. Initial workup showed no troponin elevation and only minor, non-ischemic EKG changes. He was admitted for observation and underwent coronary angiography, which revealed no new significant coronary disease or stent issues. His admission creatinine was elevated at 1.5, consistent with acute kidney injury likely due to dehydration, but improved to baseline with IV fluid administration. He remained chest pain-free during hospitalization, and all home medications were continued without change. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up with his primary care physician and cardiologist.
problems: Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery with unspecified angina pectoris
Disorder of the autonomic nervous system, unspecified
Personal history of transient ischemic attack (TIA), and cerebral infarction without residual deficits
Presence of coronary angioplasty implant and graft
